Earlier this year, Apple launched the MacBook Neo laptop, catching the personal computer market off guard. Although the aggressive pricing strategy of that notebook was subsequently adjusted according to market conditions, it took Windows阵营 rivals several months to gradually unveil their counterattack products. HP has today joined the fray, launching a new laptop equipped with an OLED display, also priced from US$699 — though there are quite a few limitations behind this price.

Overall, the HP OmniBook 5 14 looks like a colourful, budget version of the MacBook Neo body, with colour schemes reminiscent of the more refined, understated green and blue tones of the Apple iPad Air lineup. Beneath its 14-inch display, the chassis is just 11.77mm thick and weighs only 2.56 pounds — though it would be quite suitable for the back-to-school season, HP somehow missed that window. The real highlight of this machine is its 14-inch screen — at this price point, you would normally only see IPS panels, but this time two OLED options are offered for consumers to choose from, with detailed specifications to be announced later. On each side of the chassis there is a full-function USB-C port and a headphone jack; opening the screen reveals an FHD camera that supports Windows Hello.

Regarding hardware specifications, HP said this laptop can support up to an Intel Core 7 processor, but the models on display only offer a single configuration. The battery life on the spec sheet is quite impressive — up to 42 hours of local video playback (battery capacity not listed) — though to be fair, local video playback tests may not reflect real-world usage. HP mentioned that this machine is compatible with its 65W GaN mini charger, which is expected to be included in the box. Apart from that, known specifications include dual microphones and audio tuned by Poly Studio; if you feel there is still quite a lot of information missing, you are absolutely not the only one with that feeling.

Firstly, the processor model for this laptop's US$700 version has still not been announced, making it difficult to compare directly with the Apple A18 Pro. HP also chose not to disclose any storage or memory configuration information — not even the 'maximum' configuration numbers — which directly reflects the enormous pressure facing the PC market amid the current memory supply crunch. Even the most eye-catching selling point comes with a fatal trade-off: HP spent considerable time at the launch event introducing the 2.5K OLED display, but that version will not ship until March 2027. The model going on sale later this month at Best Buy comes with a 2K OLED display, but the brightness drops sharply from 650 nits to just 300 nits.

Taking all the unlisted details above, as well as some disappointing answers, if HP has still managed to pique your interest, please keep a close eye on more information to be released before the product officially goes on sale.
